title: The Song Returns to Zoe
subtitle: Where the verses are given away, not kept

intro.text: You come down the mountain carrying five whole pages, and the land of Zoe is still dim.
Of course it is. The verses were never yours to keep, Believer. They were yours to carry back.
Carry them, then. Carry them alone. That has always been enough for you.
It has never once been enough. Not for anyone. Read them out loud, and let the others read them back.

levels.title: Reading Aloud in the Square
levels.setting: The village square, one week later

dialogue.text: Read it! Read the first one! I want to hear what a whole verse sounds like!
Everyone's here. Even the ones who stopped coming to the well.
Read it, Believer — and let them finish it with you. A verse two people know is twice as hard to tear.

levels.mission: Restore the verse the whole village will learn together.

puzzle.verse: This is the ____ which the LORD hath made; we will ____ and be glad in it.
hints: The first blank is the one you are standing in.
The second blank is the verb that fills a square with singing.
puzzle.reveal: "This is the day which the LORD hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it." — Psalm 118:24

levels.title: The Village Lattice
levels.setting: The chapel wall, where the verses are painted

dialogue.text: I've started painting them on the chapel wall. Across, and down, so they hold each other up.
Paint will fade. Stone will crack. You are decorating a ruin.
Then let us make the ruin say something true while it stands. Rebuild the lattice, Believer.
I'll hold the paint! I'm good at holding paint!

levels.mission: Rebuild the lattice painted on the chapel wall.

clues.clue: "Be ____, and know that I am God"

hints: STILL is the top row again — stillness keeps coming back.
REFUGE crosses HOSTS, and TROUBLE runs across the fourth row.
puzzle.reveal: "Be still, and know that I am God… The LORD of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge." — Psalm 46:10-11

levels.title: The Pages, Given Away
levels.setting: The square, the morning of the giving

dialogue.text: The next morning you tear the five pages into thirty pieces and hand one to every person in the square.
You have destroyed them. You have given away the only weapon you had.
Weapon? No. Seed. Put the promise back in the order it was first given, Believer.
My piece says 'love'. Just that. One word, and I've never needed it more.

levels.mission: Rebuild the promise as it is handed from person to person.

puzzle.prompt: Arrange the promise as it was first spoken.
hints: It begins with consideration, not instruction.
Love comes before works, never after.
puzzle.reveal: "And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works." — Hebrews 10:24

levels.title: The Last Dark Corner
levels.setting: Under the chapel, where the Shadow retreated

dialogue.text: One corner of Zoe is still dark. Under the chapel, where the Shadow went to wait out the singing.
One corner, Believer. You have never once managed a whole land. Not in thirty levels.
And I only need one corner. I have always only needed one corner.
Then take even that from it. Find the words hiding in the dark under the chapel.
I'll bring the forge light. It's brighter than it used to be.

levels.mission: Match the word pairs in the last dark corner.

puzzle.reference: The words that end the story
hints: Find each matching pair of words.
Remember where you saw each word.
puzzle.reveal: Worship, sing, rise, shine, life — the last dark corner has nothing left to hold. Zoe is singing again.

levels.title: The Song of Zoe
levels.setting: The village square, dusk, the whole land restored

dialogue.text: At dusk the whole land is lit — not by torches, but by the sound of thirty people reading at once.
I will be back tomorrow. I am always back tomorrow. That has never failed me.
And we will be here tomorrow, with the words already in our mouths. That has never failed us.
Believer! Sing the last one! The one you've been building the whole time!
We know our piece. You say yours, and we'll say it back.
Thirty levels, Believer. One more word.
So finish the verse that was torn out on your very first morning in the square. Finish the song of Zoe.

levels.mission: Restore the verse the whole story has been building toward.

puzzle.verse: For I the LORD thy God will hold thy right ____, saying unto thee, Fear not; I will ____ thee.
hints: The first blank is the one He holds, and it is also where the sun rises.
The second blank is three promises long in the original verse.
puzzle.reveal: "For I the LORD thy God will hold thy right hand, saying unto thee, Fear not; I will help thee." — Isaiah 41:13. The song of Zoe never stops. It only waits for someone to read it aloud.
